title: Pluggable A/B Sandbox: traffic fencing, adaptive exposure policies, and sequential hypothesis checks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: teams lack a standardized, composable A/B testing sandbox that combines fine-grained exposure control (canary/traffic fencing), shadow routing, and robust sequential statistical checks for model version comparison. Current experiments are ad-hoc: infra work is duplicated, early-stop rules are inconsistent, and product owners cannot confidently rely on automated rollback triggers.

Proposed solution: build a Pluggable A/B Sandbox that provides: (1) an experiment DSL and API for defining variants, exposure policies, and traffic fences; (2) runtime primitives to route percentage or cohort-based traffic, shadow selected requests to candidate variants, and enforce hard quotas per-customer or global; (3) a statistical controller implementing group-sequential and alpha-spending strategies (optional SPRT-like early stopping) with configurable metrics and thresholds; (4) an automatic rollback/autorestore policy engine that triggers based on multi-metric signals and risk budgets; and (5) Console workflows and REST endpoints for creating, monitoring, and approving experiments.

Scope: MVP covers model-version A/B and canary flows for text-generation endpoints (hosted + dedicated); includes console experiment builder, server-side exposure enforcement, sequential test engine (Wald-SPRT and group-sequential options), telemetry dashboards, and an initial set of pre-defined safety guards (latency, error-rate, toxicity regressions).

Non-goals: full cross-product experimentation (feature flags), deep multi-armed bandit auto-allocation, or complex customer-level personalization in MVP.
acceptance_criteria: API: create/update/delete experiment definitions with variants, exposure schedules, and rollback policies
Runtime: traffic fencing enforces variant exposure within 1% of target at p99 under production load
Stats: sequential controller computes p-values and stopping decisions in <5s per evaluation window and records decisions to event log
Console: UX to start an experiment, view metric deltas, and manually approve or abort rollouts
Rollback: automatic rollback triggers when two of three monitored signals breach configured thresholds for 3 consecutive evaluation windows
Observability: dashboards show variant-level latency, token-cost, error-rate, and custom user-defined metrics with historical comparisons
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP, 4 weeks): API + runtime primitives + stats engine + console create/view. Limit to internal staging traffic and a small set of partner customers. Phase 2 (2 weeks): expand to production hosts, add shadow routing toggle and customer quotas. Phase 3 (2 weeks): tighten auto-rollback heuristics, add canary presets, and onboard 3 pilot teams. Finalize security review and compliance before GA release in console-2025.04.
metrics: performance: median latency and p99 latency
cost: tokens per request and cost delta
statistical_checks: Sequential testing harness supports two strategies: (A) Group-sequential with configurable alpha-spending function (O'Brien-Fleming and Pocock presets), and (B) Wald SPRT for binary pass/fail signals. Platform computes cumulative test statistics per evaluation window, emits decisions (continue/stop/rollback) and stores full history for offline audit. Users can select one-sided or two-sided tests, set minimum sample sizes, and define effect size targets. All statistical outputs must be accompanied by confidence intervals and pre-registered hypothesis metadata.
api_changes: Add /experiments endpoints: POST /experiments (definition + targets + policies), GET /experiments/{id}/status, POST /experiments/{id}/control (pause/resume/abort), and /experiments/{id}/metrics for raw observations. Request/response schemas documented in the API changelog. New headers for shadow-routing: X-Redwood-Experiment: <id>:<variant>.
console_changes: Experiment creation wizard with: variant selector (model version), exposure schedule (percent + cohorts), safety gates (metric thresholds), and rollback policy builder. New experiment detail page with time-series comparison, stat-test panel (including p-values and alpha spending chart), and a transcript of decision events. Admin-only controls for manual rollback and customer-targeted fencing.
infra_tasks: ENG-19821: runtime routing primitives + low-latency variant selection
ENG-20145: eventing pipeline for experiment telemetry (Kafka topics, schema updates)
ENG-20600: stats-service implementation and persistence of interim results
risks: False positives from multiple sequential looks if alpha spending misconfigured
Runtime correctness under bursty traffic could briefly exceed exposure budgets without careful token-bucket shaping
Customer data residency concerns when evaluating cross-region metrics (need aggregation controls)
Auto-rollback misfires causing customer-visible regressions if metrics are noisy
